finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the `f` query parameter is joined onto the root without any containment check, so `../` sequences escape /srv/files and let an unauthenticated caller read arbitrary files the process can access.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl (r.URL.Query().Get("f"), files.go:12), attacker-controlled and unauthenticated
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered with no authentication or middleware
filepath.Join calls Clean, which resolves `..` lexically and yields /etc/passwd, outside /srv/files; ReadFile reads it
file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no prefix check after Clean (e.g. strings.HasPrefix against root+separator), no os.Root/fs.ValidPath, no allow-list, no auth. The only error handling is NotFound on a read failure. Symlinks are not resolved either. By contrast, avatar() at files.go:22 uses filepath.Base, which blocks traversal there; I checked it and it is not vulnerable. Base('..') gives /srv/files/avatars/.., a directory, so ReadFile fails.

verdict.guard_found: none (filepath.Join only cleans lexically; no Base, prefix check, auth or allow-list on /dl)
verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw `f` query value to os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no containment check, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves outside /srv/files and files.go:18 returns the contents to an unauthenticated caller of the /dl route registered at files.go:32.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw `f` query value to filepath.Join(root, name), and Join only cleans the path lexically, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves outside /srv/files; files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth and files.go:18 writes the file contents to the response.
